question: Does HiveMind's MoE LoRA add-on lower next-token loss of the frozen base Vxtzq/Crowd-v1 on real rows that neither training nor the training ratchet's evaluation ever read?

moe.description: the same base, upcycled in place, with the checkpoint's buckets loaded

arms.newer_checkpoints: not used, even if they appear during the run

data.lineage_manifests_identical: runs 20261116T085412Z, 20261116T104052Z, 20261118T052031Z, 20261118T101755Z (the checkpoint's whole lineage) list the same heldout_rows/train_rows for every source
data.test_row_rule: For each trained expert (manifest order) and each of its sources (manifest order), test rows start at that source's train_rows[1] (the first row after the last row training read) and are scanned in increasing order, at most 2000 rows per source. Rows are fetched by the source's manifest origin: local_hf_cache -> hivemind.swarm.crowdgpt_real_shards.LocalHFCacheFetcher (file order, same as training); datasets_server -> fetch_rows_datasets_server, 100 rows per request. A later source of the same expert is read only if the earlier ones give fewer than chunks_per_expert chunks. A source with no rows at or after train_rows[1] is reported as exhausted; an expert with no chunks is reported as skipped and never substituted.

expected_skips.E3_formal_logic_arc: no source (every source is a benchmark); not trained
expected_skips.E4_physics_stem: maximus-21/PhysicsQA has 370 rows (datasets-server /size) and train_rows end at 370: no unseen rows

data.row_order_check: Before registration: for every local_hf_cache source, rows [train_end-100, train_end) read now through LocalHFCacheFetcher equal the training run's cached rows JSON, and no cached block starts at train_end (all 4 sources matched on 2026-11-18). The script repeats this check and aborts on a mismatch.
data.text_and_tokens: text = crowdgpt_real_shards.row_to_text(row); ids = Crowd-v1 tokenizer.encode(text).ids (same calls as training)

chunking.rule: one chunk per test row: the first 64 token ids of a row with at least 64 ids; rows with fewer ids are skipped

metric.per_chunk: mean next-token NLL (nats) over the 63 shifted positions of the chunk, batch size 1, model.eval(), torch.no_grad()
metric.paired_difference: d_i = NLL_moe_i - NLL_base_i (negative = the add-on lowers loss)
metric.compute: CPU only (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty, asserted in-process), fp32 trunk weights, torch.set_num_threads(4), nice 19
metric.base_equivalence_gate: after the base arm, the model is upcycled in place with the split above and zero-delta (fresh) buckets; its NLL on chunk 0 must match the dense NLL within 1e-3 nats, else the run aborts before the MoE arm

statistics.primary: paired bootstrap of mean(d): i.i.d. resampling of chunks with replacement, 10000 resamples, numpy.random.default_rng(20261118), percentile 95% CI (2.5, 97.5)
secondary_reported: per-expert mean base NLL, mean MoE NLL, mean d and relative change
exact two-sided sign test on d (ties dropped), informational only

decision_rule.INSUFFICIENT_N: fewer than 200 chunks in total: no decision
decision_rule.PASS: CI upper bound < 0 (the add-on lowers held-out loss)
decision_rule.HARM: CI lower bound > 0 (the add-on raises held-out loss)
decision_rule.domain_guard: B3 (docs/MVP_TARGET.md) also needs no domain worse than +1%: guard holds when every evaluated expert has mean NLL_moe <= 1.01 * mean NLL_base
decision_rule.b3_effect: This evaluation supports B3 only if verdict == PASS and the domain guard holds. Any other outcome (NO_GAIN, HARM, INSUFFICIENT_N, or PASS with a failed guard) leaves B3 failing. The verdict is reported as the rule gives it, whatever it is.

scorecard: scripts/mvp_scorecard.py check_b3 reads only artifacts/experiments/GRANITE_ADAPTER_*gate*.json; it has no hook for this receipt, so the scorecard wiring is not changed by this experiment.
receipt: artifacts/experiments/E_B3_MOE_PAIRED_<date>.json, carrying this spec's sha256, the pre-registration commit, the script commit, the row indices used per source, the sha256 of the chunk token ids, per-chunk NLLs, start/end times and a deviations list
